title: Crate config

act2.summary: insulated export crates arrive - one new optional field, and one cross-field rule that has nothing to do with which material family was chosen

solutions.title: A fluent CrateSpecBuilder, one step per field
solutions.tradeoff: A new field means a new fluent step: a private field, an .insulated() method, a line in the constructor's destructuring, a line in the validation, a line in the return - and both call sites in crate-spec.ts need the new .insulated(insulated) link added to their chains. That's the most files, the most lines and the most hunks of any route, including the no-pattern baseline: the ceremony that pays off when a crate has many optional, order-independent fields to assemble buys nothing when the change is one field threaded through unconditionally.

solutions.title: A CrateFamily per material, supplying the one product that varies by material
solutions.tradeoff: Insulation has nothing to do with which family supplies the fastener - it cuts across both families equally. So the family classes (WoodCrateFamily, PlasticCrateFamily) need no change at all; only assembleCrate's shared validation grows the new check, same as the object-literal route's shared function. Measured byte-for-byte identical to object-literal on every dimension: the family axis this pattern protects isn't the axis this act 2 varies along, so it costs exactly what walking away from the pattern costs - not more, but not less either.

solutions.title: A material-to-fastener lookup plus one shared validator function
solutions.tradeoff: One shared assembleCrate function means the new field and its validation are written once and reused by both buildExportCrate and buildDomesticCrate. Cheapest route measured, tied exactly with Abstract Factory - the no-pattern baseline, which duplicates its validation across both functions instead of sharing it, pays for the same check twice and comes in a line more expensive.

reviewFocus: Does the chosen candidate's WALKTHROUGH.md name what would change my mind about the choice, or does it just describe the code?
Is 'insulation cuts across material, so the family axis doesn't help here' a fair reading of why Abstract Factory doesn't pay off on this act 2?
In the builder route, is the new .insulated() step actually optional - does calling buildDomesticCrate still produce an uninsulated crate with no code path touching the new rule?
Do all three routes - and the no-pattern baseline - agree, byte for byte, on which combinations of material and maxLoadKg are rejected once insulation is in play?
Would a reader's CHOICE.md, written before act 2, have predicted that the axis this exercise tests (material family) isn't the axis act 2 actually varies along (insulated vs not)?
